quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Why Peak Tickets Cost More] Rail companies charge higher fares at rush hour for a practical reason, not just to make money. Trains are fullest between 7 and 9 a.m., and extra carriages are expensive to run for only two hours a day. By making peak travel pricier, companies encourage flexible passengers to travel later, which spreads the crowd across more trains. Passengers who can start work at ten often save a surprising amount.
quests.question: What is the main reason for higher peak fares?
options: To reduce crowding on the busiest trains
To pay for building new railway stations
To reward passengers who travel regularly
To discourage people from long journeys
quests.correctAnswer: To reduce crowding on the busiest trains
quests.hint: Think about what the companies hope flexible passengers will do.
quests.explanation: Higher fares push flexible passengers to travel later, which spreads the crowd across more trains.
quests.evidenceLine: encourage flexible passengers to travel later
